title: Segment group limits, microtenant scope and managed groups

prose.text: This subject covers segment group limits, microtenant scope and groups that Deception manages.

prose.label: Microtenants.
prose.text: Microtenant admins manage segment groups, and a custom microtenant can still use Default Microtenant groups in policies: [[zpa.microtenants.isolation:managed-config]], [[zpa.microtenants.admin-permissions:default-resources-usable]]. {{microtenant-field}} {{shared-microtenant-ids-field}} Visibility and sharing are open {{gap:microtenant-visibility}}. Application segment sharing is in [[zpa.microtenants.share-and-move]].

prose.label: Managed groups.
prose.text: {{deception-locked}} What the API does is open {{gap:deception-api-effect}}.

checks.do: How many segment groups the tenant holds against the limit before proposing a restructuring that adds groups.
Whether the group is managed by Deception, which removes the console edit and delete options.
Which microtenant the group is defined in, and what permission a custom microtenant has on groups defined in the Default Microtenant.

group-limit.statement: The Ranges & Limitations article lists a limit of 200 segment groups.

microtenant-field.statement: A segment group carries `microtenantId` and `microtenantName`, and the Terraform doc says `microtenant_id` requires the microtenant license and feature flag, or the `ZPA_MICROTENANT_ID` environment variable.

quotes: The attribute ``microtenant_id`` is optional and requires the microtenant license and feature flag enabled for the respective tenant.
The provider also supports the microtenant ID configuration via the environment variable `ZPA_MICROTENANT_ID` which is the recommended method.

shared-microtenant-ids-field.statement: The v1 segment group body in the API spec carries a `sharedMicrotenantIds` list.

deception-locked.statement: If a segment group is configured using Zscaler Deception, the console's edit and delete options are unavailable.

quotes: If a segment group is configured using Zscaler Deception, then the edit and delete options are unavailable.

policy-migrated-field.statement: A segment group carries a `policyMigrated` boolean in the API spec, the Go model and the Python model.

quotes: self.policy_migrated = config["policyMigrated"] if "policyMigrated" in config else None

microtenant-visibility.title: Visibility and sharing of segment groups across microtenants
microtenant-visibility.blocks: saying whether a group in one microtenant can be referenced from another microtenant's policies or shared like an application segment
microtenant-visibility.detail: The help documents sharing for application segments, and the v1 group body has sharedMicrotenantIds, but no source states group sharing or visibility rules. Unverified legacy statements: a group created in Microtenant A is not visible to Microtenant B's admin and cannot be referenced in B's policy rules; the default microtenant admin sees all microtenant groups; when the microtenant license is not active microtenant_id is ignored.

deception-api-effect.title: What the API does when a Deception-managed segment group is changed
deception-api-effect.blocks: saying Terraform or SDK changes to such a group fail
deception-api-effect.detail: Unverified legacy statement: attempting to modify these groups through Terraform or the SDK results in an API error, and they are managed from the Deception admin portal. The help states only that the console edit and delete options are unavailable.

policy-migrated-meaning.title: What policyMigrated records
policy-migrated-meaning.blocks: setting or relying on the flag
policy-migrated-meaning.detail: Unverified legacy statement: policyMigrated appears to track whether legacy policy migration has been run on the group and should be treated as read-only and not set programmatically. No captured help article describes the field.
